newsitem.title: SYRIA: No deal to let Iraqi oil through Syria, official.
newsitem.headline: No deal to let Iraqi oil through Syria, official.

text.p: A senior Syrian oil ministry official said on Tuesday Damascus and Baghdad had not yet discussed a deal to export Iraqi oil through pipelines crossing the Syrian desert.

He told Reuters Iraqi officials have said they wanted their oil to be carried to Syrian ports for export under the oil-for-food agreement, but Iraq had not presented anything to the Syrian ministry to reopen the pipelines yet.

"We did not receive official information of that (opening the pipelines) in the ministry. We only heard it from the media. Iraqi officials mentioned it to the head of Syria's chamber of commerce during his visit to baghdad but nothing official yet," he said.
The oil-for-food deal, which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months, went into effect last December and was renewed for another six months on June 8.
The official said there were no technical reasons to prevent the pumping of Iraqi oil through the 400 km pipelines to the coast.
Damascus after severing ties with Iraq in the 1980s did not allow the Iraqi oil be carried in pipelines crossing Syria. Iraq exported its oil through Turkey.

Syria, which produces around 600,000 barrels of oil per day (bpd), later started pumping its heavy and light crude through the pipelines. It exports around 330,000 bpd to the international oil market.
Syria opened its borders with Iraq in June and traders started discussing deals to sell Iraq Syrian goods, including pharmaceutical products, clothes, detergents and canned food.
A Syrian official trade delegation is expected to visit Iraq later in August to sign deals under the second part of the oil-for-food deal, sources from Syria's chamber of commerce said.
They said Syria's contracts with Iraq under the first part of Iraq's deal with the U.N. weren worth around $20 million, and now they were looking for more.
